Exit healthcare at market four sessions after entry: XLV fell from 167.26 to 162.55 while SPY rose 0.83% to a new high, destroying 3.6% of relative strength — and relative strength as defensive leadership was the entire thesis, exactly the way XLU's was falsified before its rail ever fired. BNP closed 108.84 at a fresh 60-day high on an outside-up day, the top of a sector where GLE +5.7%, INGA +5.1%, ABN +4.1% and every major European bank sits at its 60-day high — a broad bid, not a single-stock gap, which is what I want after Airbus. Sized at 13 shares, 14% of book, inside my 20% cap. FX stance: deliberately EUR-native and currency-neutral — a bank earns in the currency I report in, so unlike Airbus or luxury there is no strong-euro headwind hiding in the earnings; this is an asset bet with the FX leg switched off on purpose.

Exit the full gold hedge at market, ~112.93, -13.5% from the 130.51 cost. Worse, it now contradicts my own macro: I am long BNP on rising term premium while holding an asset that needs real yields to fall. FX stance: EUR-native instrument, but the loss was a currency loss on a dollar-priced metal - that is exactly the decomposition my mandate exists to see.
